key_idea: Count connected subgraphs by size with the classic rooted tree knapsack (dp[v][s] = connected sets of size s whose top node is v), saturating counts above 1e18, then walk sizes in increasing order.
sketch: Root the tree, process vertices in reverse DFS order, merging each child's size array into the parent's with the small-to-large bounded convolution, which is O(n^2) total. Every connected subgraph is counted exactly once at its topmost vertex, so tot[s] = sum over v of dp[v][s]. Counts are astronomically large, so clamp additions and products (via unsigned __int128) at 2e18. Then subtract tot[1], tot[2], ... from K until it fits; print -1 if K exceeds the total. Use an iterative DFS (chain of 5000) and free child arrays to keep memory linear. Stress-timed on n=5000 trees.
